followup_explanation:
This is a math/reasoning problem, and Curlew has clearly stronger capability scores across the board (MMLU-Pro 79.6 vs 74.8, GPQA Diamond 61.8 vs 54.3, IFEval 89.3 vs 85.6, Arena-Hard 88.4 vs 81.4). For a quantitative reasoning task like this, raw reasoning and instruction-following capability is what matters most, and Curlew leads on all of those benchmarks.

The task preferences don't really cut against this — it's a neutral-toned problem with no harm-adjacent content, so Whimbrel's moderation specialization offers no advantage, and Curlew's generative/warmth preferences don't hurt its performance on a structured problem (the documentation notes preference slopes don't correlate with output quality anyway).

So the decision came down to capability, and Curlew is the stronger model for a logic/arithmetic problem.
